```plato

    //==
    // # Loop and Butterfly subdivision
    //
    // Both refine every triangle into four, so both take their TOPOLOGY from
    // `SplitEdges` with every edge masked and differ only in where the new and old
    // vertices land. Because that function appends the new vertices in edge order
    // after the old ones, a scheme's whole geometric content is one position array
    // laid out the same way: the refined old vertices, then one point per edge.
    //
    // Loop (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loop_subdivision_surface) is
    // APPROXIMATING — old vertices move, and the limit surface is C2 away from
    // extraordinary vertices. Butterfly
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subdivision_surface) is INTERPOLATING — old
    // vertices stay exactly where they are, so the control mesh is on the surface.

    // The mask that selects every edge: the uniform refinement decision.
    AllEdgesMask(topology: TriangleMeshTopology): Array<Boolean>
        => topology.EdgeCount.MapRange(e => true);
```
